data.description:
## Incident Overview

Discovered while triaging failed per-branch reviews on PRs #160, #163, #164 in epic d076. All clean per-story PRs (1-2 file diffs) were producing reviews citing files NOT in the PR's diff (e.g., bridge-inbound.py, ticket-edit.sh) because the workflow computed the diff scope against a stale SPRINT_SESSION_ID repo variable.

Concrete root cause:
- `.github/workflows/per-branch-review.yml` line 110-111:
    BASE=$(git merge-base "origin/${SPRINT_SESSION_ID:-main}" HEAD)
    git diff "$BASE" HEAD > /tmp/story-diff.patch
- SPRINT_SESSION_ID repo variable was set to "worktree-20260515-200444" by sprint Phase A
- That branch still exists on origin but its HEAD is an OLD commit (deb229115bc4 — from before bug fixes were merged into session)
- merge-base with that old commit produces a 5492-line diff covering all session work since
- Result: reviews on small per-story PRs cite files belonging to unrelated work that landed AFTER the worktree branch HEAD

## Why the variable went stale

The session branch's effective head migrated:
- Phase A: SPRINT_SESSION_ID set to "worktree-20260515-200444"
- Phase F: created story sub-branch "story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc" via STORY_PR_BASE pattern
- PR #140 opened from "story/d076.../2abb-..." → main; session work continued accumulating on THAT branch
- Subsequent bug-fix PRs (#145, #146, #148) merged into "story/d076.../2abb-..."
- worktree-20260515-200444 was never updated

## Hardening recommendations

### 1. Authoritative-source switch (PRIMARY)
Per-branch-review.yml should look up the PR's base directly when a PR exists for the branch, rather than relying on the repo variable:
    PR_NUM=$(gh pr list --head "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
    if [[ -n "$PR_NUM" ]]; then
        BASE_REF=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUM" --json baseRefName --jq .baseRefName)
    fi
    BASE_REF="${BASE_REF:-${SPRINT_SESSION_ID:-main}}"
    BASE=$(git merge-base "origin/$BASE_REF" HEAD)

This makes the workflow self-correcting: each PR's diff is computed against ITS actual base. The repo variable becomes a fallback for branch pushes without an open PR.

### 2. Sprint lifecycle hygiene
- Phase F (or Phase I session-close) must update SPRINT_SESSION_ID when the session branch's effective head migrates to a new branch name (the 2abb-... rename case here).
- When a sprint completes or is abandoned, SPRINT_SESSION_ID should be cleared. Stale values across sessions are the failure mode this incident exposed.

### 3. Branch existence + freshness assertion
Workflow should validate that the resolved BASE branch exists and is reasonably current:
    if ! git ls-remote --exit-code origin "$BASE_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "WARN: BASE_REF $BASE_REF not on origin — falling back to main" >&2
        BASE_REF="main"
    fi

### 4. Suspicious-diff detection
A workflow that produces a 5000+ line diff for a "scoped per-story review" is almost certainly mis-scoped. Add a sanity check:
    DIFF_SIZE=$(wc -l < /tmp/story-diff.patch)
    if [[ "$DIFF_SIZE" -gt 1500 && -n "$PR_NUM" ]]; then
        echo "WARN: scoped review produced ${DIFF_SIZE}-line diff for a per-story PR — check BASE_REF resolution" >&2
    fi

### 5. Document the contract
Add a header comment in per-branch-review.yml documenting:
- What SPRINT_SESSION_ID is and when it gets set/cleared
- What the fallback chain is
- Why PR base is authoritative when available

## Immediate workaround applied during incident
Updated SPRINT_SESSION_ID via `gh api PATCH .../actions/variables/SPRINT_SESSION_ID -f value="story/d076-d35e-55db-4843/2abb-11b6-37ca-49dc"` to point at the current session branch. Workflow re-runs in progress to verify scope correction.

## Related
- Discovered during user-directed remediation pass on epic d076 (after PR #163's failed review found 4 critical findings in bridge-inbound.py despite the PR's diff only being 2 unrelated files).
data.title: [per-branch-review.yml]: SPRINT_SESSION_ID coupling -> Stale variable produces wrong-scoped reviews; PR base should be the authoritative source
